experiment: throughput under concurrency: 2000 independent task instances, 20 concurrent

host.note: dedicated box, nothing else running on it

versions.executor: CeleryExecutor (as shipped by the official compose)

fibo31_worker_container_s.note: naive recursive fibo(31) measured with time.perf_counter() inside the airflow-worker container on an otherwise idle box

cpu.basis: 20 cores / 0.134983 s of compute per task (median fibo(31))

workloads.fanout: one DAG run per rep; a single @task mapped with .expand() over a literal list of 2000 ints (dynamic task mapping). All 2000 task instances are created by the scheduler up-front and sit in 'scheduled' state before the first one starts, verified per rep: max(scheduled_dttm) <= min(start_date).

protocol.reps: 1 warmup run discarded, then 5 measured runs, per (config, workload)
protocol.order: stock/sleep, stock/cpu, then DB wiped (docker compose down -v) and the stack rebuilt for tuned/sleep, tuned/cpu
protocol.db_reset: each configuration started from an empty metadata DB so DB size could not differ between configs
protocol.metrics_source: Airflow metadata DB task_instance: queued_dttm, start_date, end_date, scheduled_dttm, state, try_number. No harness wall-clock enters any reported number.
protocol.cpu_measurement: independent 1Hz /proc/stat sampler on the host for the whole session (cpulog.tsv)

AIRFLOW_UID.why: so the bind-mounted dags/ and logs/ are writable by the host user; the official guide instructs this

compose_file_edit.why: the only edit to the official compose file; a value hardcoded in the compose 'environment:' block cannot be overridden from an env file. The default is still 'true', so the stock configuration is byte-for-byte equivalent to the published file.

core.default_pool_task_slot_count.verdict: never bound: 128 slots is far above 20

scheduler.max_tis_per_query.verdict: never reached: measured scheduler enqueue batches averaged 8.8 (stock) / 9.1-9.4 (tuned) task instances with a max of 20, so the 16-per-query cap was not the limit

core.max_active_runs_per_dag.verdict: irrelevant: one DAG run at a time

scheduler.task_queued_timeout.verdict: never hit: no task instance was stuck in 'queued'; zero retries across all 20 measured reps

api.workers.verdict: one api-server process serves the Execution API for every task runner. With a 5+10 SQLAlchemy pool it is a real control-plane bottleneck: during an early trial run, adding the harness's own api polling on top of 20 task runners produced 'QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached' and HTTP 500s. The harness was therefore changed to poll Postgres directly, and the 20 measured reps recorded zero pool timeouts.

diagnostic_concurrency_60.purpose: to establish whether the 20-way cap or Airflow's control plane bound throughput. Same tuned base, sleep workload, with core.parallelism / core.max_active_tasks_per_dag / celery.worker_concurrency all raised from 20 to 60. 1 warmup + 2 reps. Not part of the reported configurations.
diagnostic_concurrency_60.finding: Tripling the cap to 60 raised mean concurrency from 8.5 to ~36 - so Airflow does fill slots when they exist - but throughput rose only from 16.8/s to 22.5/s (+34%), because per-task exec time went from 0.50s to ~1.5s. The 20-way cap was therefore NOT what bound the reported numbers: the limit is the rate at which Airflow's control plane (scheduler critical section plus the single api-server Execution API) can start and finish task instances, roughly 17-23 task instances/s on this box regardless of the concurrency cap.

scheduler_enqueue_pattern.method: grouped task_instance.queued_dttm into bursts separated by more than 0.3s, for the last rep of each (config, workload)
scheduler_enqueue_pattern.reading: the scheduler releases work in ~9-task-instance bursts about twice a second. The batch size barely moves between stock and tuned; only the gap between bursts shrinks, which is why tuned is ~19% faster on the sleep workload and the 20 worker slots are still only ~43% occupied.

errors_and_failures.aborted_trial_run: one earlier trial of the stock series was aborted because the harness polled the REST API during the run and hit HTTP 500s from api-server DB-pool exhaustion. No measured rep comes from that trial; the stack and metadata DB were rebuilt from scratch before the reported stock series.
